hypothesis: E178 overfits the dense paired targets. Test whether a fixed low-dimensional additive card effect retains cross-family signal without contextual network memorization. This is a diagnostic comparator, not a new Heart policy.
features: Difference of actual afterstate per-card/upgraded inventory counts in native card units, plus maximum-HP difference in2HP units for Bowl. No context interactions, seed, RNG or future inputs. Unobserved fit feature columns remain exactly zero. Deterministic feature extraction and its units checked.
labels_and_roles: Exactly18682 covered E178 paired combat targets and all1536 families. Train equal total family weight, then equal covered-menu weight, then equal covered-alternative weight. Original inner/full roles; evaluate identical8192 validation/held draws per fold. Missing77 pairs remain missing.
objective: For each of2 output channels, solve weighted squared error plus ridge_strength1 times squared coefficients. Each family has total weight1. Solve once for inner and once for full fit per fold, no regularization grid or checkpoint selection. Six closed-form parameter fits are training, despite zero gradient optimizer updates.
gate: Same auxiliary screen as E178: mean held two-channel MSE at most90percent of zero-difference baseline, every fold better. A pass only supports a stable additive auxiliary effect, not a Heart policy or adopted model; a failure closes this fixed main-effect recipe without a regularization scan.
limits: Relative effects at the first subsequent audited mapped combat, including intervening parent decisions and possible event fights. This low-dimensional additive control omits deck/relic interactions. Source labels and all families are historical development data; zero gradient updates must not be described as no fitting. No new game, Heart policy or acceptance result.
